patch_resolves_note: The official `patch.diff` did not apply to the staged vulnerable checkout, so fixed-side validation used the authoritative `n132/arvo:52006-fix` image instrumented with the same frozen assertions. In that real fixed build the added `addresses_len -= address_len;` keeps the per-TLV byte counter synchronized with the real parser `length`, so the second-iteration guard rejects the malformed subframe before any overrun discard or sink read.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: After the first address body is discarded in the CDP Addresses TLV loop, the subframe counter `addresses_len` must be updated by the same `address_len` so it stays synchronized with the real parser remainder `length` before the next address iteration.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the post-discard accounting point with `addresses_len` still 32 bytes larger than `length`, and the later second-iteration guard still executes on that stale state. The fixed original reaches the same source-grounded point with the two counters synchronized and then evaluates the second-iteration guard cleanly.
root_cause_criterion.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `address_body_discard_accounting.addresses_len_after_body_discard=64` and `length_after_body_discard=32` while `second_protocol_length_guard` still executes; the fixed trace records `32 == 32` at the same event and also executes `second_protocol_length_guard`.

nodes.state: The `PEEK_UINT16` sink reads from the same parser cursor that the second overrun discard already advanced past the end of the heap-backed frame buffer.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `second_protocol_len_discard.pos_after_discard == second_address_length_read.read_ptr`.

nodes.state: At the second-iteration `if (addresses_len < address_len + 2)` guard, the stale subframe counter still overstates the bytes remaining in the TLV after the two header-byte reads.
The second-iteration `PEEK_DISCARD(address_len)` advances `pos` beyond `frame + s`, producing the out-of-bounds parser state consumed by the later sink.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace satisfies `second_protocol_len_discard.pos_after_discard > second_protocol_len_discard.frame_end`.

edges.relation: The same `addresses_len` value left at the first address-body discard is carried into the next loop iteration before the second address header consumes its two bookkeeping bytes.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `address_body_discard_accounting.addresses_len_after_body_discard == second_protocol_length_guard.addresses_len_before_header_reads == 64`, and the fixed trace records the same relation with value 32.

edges.relation: The same `address_len` value admitted by the second-iteration guard is the span immediately used by the following `PEEK_DISCARD(address_len)`.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `second_protocol_length_guard.address_len_for_discard == second_protocol_len_discard.discard_len == 32`.

edges.relation: The parser cursor produced by the second overrun discard is reused unchanged as the base pointer of the following `PEEK_UINT16` sink read.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `second_protocol_len_discard.pos_after_discard == second_address_length_read.read_ptr`.

verification_limitations: The official `patch.diff` failed to apply to the staged checkout. Fixed-side runtime evidence therefore comes from the authoritative `n132/arvo:52006-fix` fallback image rather than an incremental patch application in the vulnerable workspace.

The reachability debugger replay observed the vulnerable assertion-event cycle twice, so `reachability_report.json` records `assertion_sequence_matches=false` even though every assertion-event breakpoint was reached in order at least once and all R1-R5 gates succeeded.
